title: Analysts: Mexican Cartels' Growing Use of Bomb-Laden Drones and IEDs Marks 'Steady Intensification of Violence'
detail: A September 5, 2026 Fortune analysis, drawing on Zacatecas state attorney general Cristian Paul Camacho's office and outside experts, reported that Zacatecas has recorded 23 explosive attacks in 2026 to date, six of them car or motorcycle bombs, with the August 30 Ojocaliente police-station car bomb (200kg of explosives, 11 injured, 60+ homes affected) the latest and largest. The piece situates the Ojocaliente attack within a broader escalation: a December Michoacán bombing blamed on CJNG killed 5 people, a 2025 Michoacán IED killed 8 soldiers, and Michoacán authorities deactivated nearly 3,200 explosive devices statewide in 2024. Vanda Felbab-Brown, an organized-crime expert at the Brookings Institution, said 'We are facing steady intensification of violence,' while Victor Manuel Sánchez, a security researcher at the Universidad Autónoma de Coahuila, and CIDE professor Carlos Pérez Ricart were also cited on the trend of cartels — chiefly CJNG and the Sinaloa Cartel — increasingly using drone-dropped and vehicle-borne explosives to contest disputed territory.

media.caption: A state police officer examines remains from the August 30 car bomb explosion outside the Ojocaliente, Zacatecas police station

confidenceReason: Single-source analytical feature (Tier-2) synthesizing official Zacatecas figures and named outside experts; the underlying Ojocaliente bombing facts are independently corroborated elsewhere, but the broader 'steady intensification' framing and cumulative explosive-attack count are this outlet's own analysis, not independently cross-checked.
